title: Not even a thorn bush (Exodus Rabbah 2:5)
hook: God speaks from a thorn bush to show no place is empty of the Presence
tomorrow: Moses asks God's name. why does the answer keep changing?

segments.voice: Yesterday: climb anyway, with fear not as the last word. Today, a man who ran away, alone in the wilderness with someone else's sheep.

Run a thumb along a blackberry cane or a rose stem and you remember fast: thorns don't look like much until they're in your skin. Moses is out in the wilderness with his father-in-law's flock when "the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush." Not a cedar. Not a palm. A scrubby thorn bush. Someone asked the rabbis: why that one?
screen: `THORNS DON'T LOOK LIKE MUCH.` → `A FLAME IN A BUSH.` → `WHY THAT ONE?`

segments.voice: Exodus Rabbah keeps the question and says who asked it: someone from outside the faith, curious, asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha why God would speak to Moses from a thorn bush. The question came from outside, and it got a straight answer: to teach you that no place is empty of the Presence, not even a thorn bush. The midrash gathers other readings too. One: the thorn bush is the lowliest of plants, and the people in Egypt were low, so God came down to where they were. The psalm says it: "I will be with him in trouble." Another notices how a thorn bush works. A hand slides in easily, but pull it out and the thorns catch, and the midrash compares that to getting into Egypt, and trying to get out. Every reading lands in the same place. The Presence doesn't wait for beautiful places. It speaks from the scratchy, the stuck, the low. And the bush burns and isn't burned up: the thorns stay thorns, and the fire is in them anyway.
screen: `WHY A THORN BUSH?` · `NO PLACE EMPTY OF THE PRESENCE.` · `LOWLY, AND GOD IS THERE.` · `EASY IN, HARD OUT.` · then, large: `NOT EVEN A THORN BUSH.`

segments.voice: Find something rough within reach: bark, a brick, the bristles of a brush, the sole of a shoe. Rest your fingertips on it, gently, and feel every snag. Let it stand for one thorny thing in your week, and keep your hand there, not pulling away, with the words: not even a thorn bush.
Not even a thorn bush: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha's answer in Exodus Rabbah. No place is empty of the Presence, not even the scratchy one.
screen: `NOT EVEN A THORN BUSH — today's word`.

segments.voice: Pocket this one: not even a thorn bush, because the fire was in the thorns. That's fifteen seventy-nine.
